lessons.title: Chapter 1 · Grammar 1 · elapsed time and new vocabulary
lessons.source: Your daily study message, checked against Chapter 1 of your uploaded textbook. No audio file was attached to this message.
corrections: 인지 → -(으)ㄴ 지 for elapsed time since an action.
한잔 (a drink) → 한참 for a long time.
출신 means origin / being from; 고향 is hometown.

entries.meaning: it has been [length of time] since …
entries.note: Attach -(으)ㄴ to a verb stem and write a space before 지. Use a duration + 되다 / 지나다. This is different from -는지 / -인지 (whether / an embedded question). Example: 한국어를 공부한 지 한 달 됐어요. = It has been one month since I started studying Korean.
After an amount or duration: 한 시간 넘게 = over an hour.
Corrected from dictated 돈으로. 돈으로 means with money / in money.
This is the 電氣 meaning; 전기 can have other meanings in other contexts.

entries.meaning: to go regularly; to attend; to commute
entries.note: 학교에 다니다 = attend school; 회사에 다니다 = work at / go regularly to a company.

entries.meaning: a long time; a good while
entries.note: Corrected from dictated 한잔. 한잔 means a drink, not a long time.
Traditionally a person from the East; East Asian in many contexts.

entries.meaning: to emigrate; to move abroad permanently
entries.note: From the country being left, English uses emigrate; immigrate describes entering the destination country.

entries.meaning: overseas Korean; a Korean living abroad
mixed ancestry; a person of mixed ancestry

Written as one word.
Also written 동북 아시아; 동북아시아 is common in geographical names.
Also written 동남 아시아.
Corrected from dictated 교회. 교회 means church.

entries.meaning: origin; being from a place, school or background
entries.note: 서울 출신 = from Seoul. 고향 is the direct word for hometown.
Original dictated spelling retained. For coworker, learn 동료.

entries.meaning: a drink; a glass of alcohol
entries.note: Original dictated spelling retained. For one cup / glass as a count, use 한 잔. For a long time, learn 한참.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 · Grammar 1 · Using Computer & Frequency adverbs
lessons.source: Your dictated study additions on 27 October 2026. You said the lesson was started today; no completion was assumed.
corrections: 전부 파일을 보내다 → 첨부 파일을 보내다 for send an attachment.
거의 means almost / nearly; 거의 + negative expresses hardly ever / almost never.
별로 + negative expresses not much / not often. 전혀 + negative expresses not at all / never.

entries.note: 타자를 치다 = to type. 타자 means typing / keystrokes.
문서를 저장하다 = save a document. 저장 = saving / storage.
파일을 삭제하다 = delete a file.
Corrected from dictated 전부 파일을 보내다. 첨부 파일 = attached file / attachment; 전부 means all.

댓글 = online comment; 댓글을 달다 = post a comment.
동영상 = video; 보다 = watch / see.
Borrowed from English download. 파일을 다운로드하다 = download a file.
블로그 = blog; 방문하다 = visit.

entries.meaning: to upload / post text or a picture
entries.note: 글을 올리다 = post some writing; 사진을 올리다 = upload a picture. 올리다 also means to raise / put up.
컴퓨터 = computer; 게임 = game; 하다 = do / play.
언제나 사용해요. = I always use it. 언제나 can also mean at any time.
늘 사용해요. = I always use it. Similar in meaning to 언제나.
가끔 사용해요. = I sometimes use it.
때때로 사용해요. = I use it from time to time.
종종 사용해요. = I use it from time to time. Similar to 가끔 and 때때로.

entries.meaning: not really / not particularly; with a negative: not often
entries.note: 별로 안 사용해요. = I do not use it much / often. 별로 is normally used with a negative expression; it does not mean rarely by itself.

entries.meaning: almost / nearly; with a negative: hardly ever / almost never
entries.note: 거의 안 사용해요. = I hardly ever use it. 거의 다 했어요. = I have almost finished. 거의 alone does not mean never.

entries.meaning: not at all; with a negative verb: never
entries.note: 전혀 사용 안 해요. = I never use it / do not use it at all. Use a negative verb for this meaning.

entries.meaning: I use both A and B.
entries.note: A와 B = A and B; 둘 다 = both. Example: 이메일과 채팅 둘 다 사용해요. = I use both email and chat.

entries.korean: A와 B 둘 다 사용 안 해요
entries.meaning: I use neither A nor B. / I do not use A or B.
entries.note: 둘 다 + a negative predicate expresses neither in this sentence. Longer negative form: A와 B 둘 다 사용하지 않아요. This is different from saying that you use only one of them.
entries.pronunciation: 에이와 비 둘 다 사용 안 해요

lessons.title: Chapter 3 · Grammar 1 · time-related expressions
lessons.source: User dictation checked against Korean Made Easy Intermediate, Chapter 3 Grammar 1, printed pp.50–53 (PDF pp.52–55); 경기 confirmed in Conversation 1 and the p.315 glossary.

entries.note: 重要: important.
Confirmed 성격이 다르다 in the p.50 example. 성격 = personality; 다르다 = to be different. Repeated twice in your dictation: marked important.
自信感: feeling confident in oneself.
30분이 지났어요. = Thirty minutes have passed. 분 uses Sino-Korean numbers: 삼십 분.
30분이 남았어요. = There are thirty minutes left.
세 시가 넘었어요. = It is past three o’clock. 시 uses native Korean numbers.
아직 세 시가 안 됐어요. = It is not three o’clock yet.
Corrected 춘분하다 → 충분하다. 시간이 충분해요. = There is enough time.
서두르다 = to hurry. -지 마세요 = please do not …
부족하다 = to be insufficient; opposite of 충분하다.

entries.meaning: to have time become available / to have free time
entries.note: 시간이 나면 전화하세요. = Call me when you have time. Write a space: 시간이 나다.

entries.meaning: to make time / set aside time

공부하는 데 시간을 써요. = I spend time studying.

entries.meaning: to save time / use time economically

entries.meaning: to use time sparingly / budget time
entries.note: 아끼다 = to spare / value; 아껴 쓰다 = to use carefully. Similar to 시간을 절약하다.
Opposite of 시간을 절약하다 / 아껴 쓰다.
맞추어 contracts to 맞춰. 약속 시간에 맞춰 오세요. = Please come at the appointed time. Textbook wording: 시간 맞춰 (가다/오다).

entries.meaning: to coordinate one’s schedule with someone
entries.note: 친구하고 시간을 맞췄어요. = I coordinated a time with my friend. 시간을 is the object; 맞추다 is an action.

entries.meaning: to delay / move a time later

entries.meaning: to go / come exactly on time

entries.meaning: not to talk / not to talk about something

referenceEntries.title: N 같은 거 · giving examples
referenceEntries.text:
N 같은 거 means “things like N / something like N.” 거 is the conversational form of 것. It gives examples rather than making an exhaustive list.

저는 과자 같은 거 안 좋아해요.
I do not like things like snacks.

불고기나 갈비 같은 거를 자주 먹어요.
I often eat things like bulgogi or galbi.

거를 is conversational; 같은 것을 is a fuller form.

referenceEntries.title: 그래요? / 그래요. · reaction and agreement
referenceEntries.text:
그래요? (rising intonation) = Really? / Is that so? It can express surprise or check what someone has said.
A: 저 내일 한국에 가요. = I am going to Korea tomorrow.
B: 그래요? = Really?

그래요. (falling intonation) = Okay. / All right. Used to accept a suggestion or agree.
A: 같이 점심 먹을까요? = Shall we have lunch together?
B: 그래요. 같이 먹어요. = Okay. Let’s eat together.

Context and intonation matter; 그래요 can also mean “that is so / that is right.”

referenceEntries.title: -(으)ㄹ까요?
referenceEntries.text:
Shall I …? / Shall we …? Ask about doing something or suggest doing it together.

After a consonant: -을까요? 먹다 → 먹을까요?
After a vowel or ㄹ: -ㄹ까요? 가다 → 갈까요? 만들다 → 만들까요?

제가 도와드릴까요? = Shall I help you?
같이 갈까요? = Shall we go together?

It can also ask for a guess/opinion depending on context: 내일 비가 올까요? = Do you think it will rain tomorrow?

referenceEntries.title: -는 것 / -(으)ㄴ 것 · noun phrases (-ing / the thing that …)
referenceEntries.text:
A modifier + 것 creates a noun phrase: “doing …” or “the thing that …”.

Verbs, present action/situation: -는 것
먹는 것 = eating / the thing one eats
한국어를 공부하는 것을 좋아해요. = I like studying Korean.

Verbs, past/completed action: -(으)ㄴ 것
먹은 것 = what one ate / the thing one has eaten
어제 산 것 = what I bought yesterday

Adjectives, present description: -(으)ㄴ 것
좋은 것 = a good thing; 예쁜 것 = a pretty thing
With adjectives this is normally a present description, not past tense.

Nouns use 인 것: 학생인 것 = being a student.
있다/없다 use -는 in modifiers: 재미있는 것, 맛없는 것.

Common contractions: 것이 → 게; 것은 → 건; 것을 → 걸.

referenceEntries.title: 것이 → 게 · 것은 → 건
referenceEntries.text:
In conversation, 것 + a particle often contracts:
것이 → 게 (subject)
것은 → 건 (topic)
것을 → 걸 (object)

공부하는 것이 좋아요. → 공부하는 게 좋아요.
Studying is good / I like studying (depending on context).

제가 좋아하는 것은 책이에요. → 제가 좋아하는 건 책이에요.
What I like is books.

한국어를 배우는 것을 좋아해요. → 한국어를 배우는 걸 좋아해요.
I like learning Korean.

건 is the contraction of 것은; it is not 곤.

referenceEntries.title: 이다 + -아/어서 → -(이)라서
referenceEntries.text:
When a noun + 이다 gives the reason (“because … is …”), this lesson uses -(이)라서.

After a noun ending in a consonant: 이라서
학생이라서 = because I am a student

After a noun ending in a vowel: 라서
친구라서 = because we are friends

Examples:
학생이라서 할인을 받아요. = I get a discount because I am a student.
친구라서 도와줬어요. = I helped because we are friends.

The cause comes first. With verbs/adjectives, use -아/어서 (바빠서, 먹어서); 하다 becomes 해서. For the causal pattern taught here, do not put -았/었- or -겠- immediately before -아/어서: 어제 아파서 못 갔어요.

Noun forms 이어서/여서 also exist; -(이)라서 is the form highlighted in this chapter.

referenceEntries.title: -기로 하다
referenceEntries.text:
To decide to do something / agree or promise to do something. Attach -기로 to a verb stem.

가다 → 가기로 하다 = decide to go
만나다 → 만나기로 하다 = agree to meet

내일 만나기로 했어요. = We decided to meet tomorrow.
오늘부터 운동하기로 해요. = Let’s decide to exercise starting today.

You can replace 하다 with 약속하다 (promise), 결정하다 / 정하다 (decide), or 결심하다 (resolve).
예: 담배를 끊기로 결심했어요. = I resolved to quit smoking.

-기로 했어요 normally reports an earlier decision; -기로 해요 can establish a decision or agreement now. The pattern is -기로 하다, not 결호하다.

referenceEntries.title: -지요 / -죠
referenceEntries.text:
-죠 is the conversational contraction of -지요. Use it to confirm something, ask for agreement, or remind the listener of a fact you expect them to know. Intonation and context matter.

우리 내일 만나기로 했죠? = We agreed to meet tomorrow, right?
오늘 춥죠? = It is cold today, isn’t it?
네, 그렇죠. = Yes, that’s right.

The past tense may come before it: 했지요? → 했죠? The 죠 ending itself does not mean “become” or “decide”; the rest of the sentence carries that meaning.

Verb/adjective stem + 지요; noun + 이지요 (consonant) / 지요 (vowel).
